A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The earlier Appendix D is retained as Appendix E in v3; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original modal-category classification, model-development analyses, human-response modeling, feature correlations, and generation-steering results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds feature-ablation experiments for human-response modeling in Appendix D and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The modal difference vector construction, projection classifiers, logistic-regression models, and steering procedure are unchanged. The new feature removals are experimental ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Dataset, task, and population coverage is unchanged. The new ablations reuse the existing human-categorization tasks from Hu et al. (2025b), Hu et al. (2025a), and Goulding et al. (2024).

E2.justification: Probability, Principal Component, and Random remain the comparison methods in Studies 1 and 3; the unsteered control also remains unchanged. Figure 9 introduces feature-ablation conditions rather than additional baseline methods.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds controlled comparisons between the full three-feature regression model and models omitting each feature individually, evaluated using the existing three metrics. Previously stated splits, model configurations, training settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused necessity analysis for Study 3: individually removing probable-improbable, improbable-impossible, and impossible-inconceivable features across its three datasets. Existing developmental, adversarial, and steering analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly specifies paired t-tests against the full-feature condition, with Bonferroni correction within each dataset, and Figure 9 adds significance markers. Neither version reports repeated-run counts or seeds; no increase in runs is established.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds ablation results: every feature removal worsens overall correlation and MSE on Hu et al. (2025b), while entropy correlation decreases when probable-improbable is removed and increases when either other feature is removed. No significant effects are reported for the two binary tasks. Existing figures and tables retain their results.

T1.justification: Modal-category definitions and the vector-construction and projection mathematics are unchanged. The added empirical analysis introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, research questions, and concluding discussion retain the same main contributions and claims. The added ablations support the existing human-categorization claim without redefining its scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix D newly interpret all three features as necessary for fine-grained categorization, but subsets as sufficient for binary judgments. They also identify a particular role for probable-improbable in predicting response entropy. Existing interpretations and applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, regression hyperparameters, steering settings, and the code-access link are unchanged. The Tuckute dataset's feature descriptions move intact from Appendix D to Appendix E; no additional implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged. Reference entries move between pages but are neither added nor removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short results paragraph in Section 5.2 and a feature-ablation appendix, renumbers the former Appendix D as E, and updates its cross-reference. The remaining prose and main section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 9 with ablation conditions, error bars, and significance markers. Existing figures and tables retain their content, with local repositioning and reflow, including Tables 3–4 sharing pages with the relocated feature descriptions.

improvement.justification: Unlike v2, v3 directly tests whether Study 3 needs each selected feature. Appendix D and Figure 9 provide useful controlled evidence and corrected significance tests, modestly strengthening the validation. However, nonsignificant effects on the binary tasks do not establish the claimed sufficiency of feature subsets, limiting the strength of that interpretation.
